scope: Bounded incremental correctness, allocation and elapsed observation; not a statistical performance comparison or formal release acceptance.
inputs: 100 deterministic pages, 12 links each, fixed timestamp, direct MarkdownPost construction, one process per receipt, off before on, no warmup, one pass.
codeIdentity: Receipts were built with worktree changes on the recorded base commits. Exact product/harness assembly hashes identify measured binaries; do not label these as builds of the final integration commit.
counters: MarkdownParseCount counts LithoMarkdownCompiler only, not direct post-edit Syntamark analysis. Before receipt HtmlParseCount counts BuildHtmlFacts sharing only and does not include 100 mandatory direct HTML parses per on-stage. After receipt separates AgentValidationDirectParseCount, AgentValidationCacheParseCount, and AgentValidationCacheHitCount.
observations: All eight stages passed output-byte/cache/parse-bound checks in both receipts. All 1200 public cross-links were checked.
After reuse: on warm/no-op has 0 compiler parses, 0 validation parses, 100 facts cache hits, 0 regenerated nodes, and unchanged output hashes. Single edit reparses/regenerates one HTML/Markdown page.
On warm allocated bytes decreased from 103735872 to 46119376. Elapsed time was 584.08 ms before and 710.9202 ms after; no speedup or regression-free claim is supported by these single observations.

Actual artifact reads and current plan/graph checks remain mandatory. Fact deserialization/cache I/O and feature planning remain additional costs. Quality-enabled JSON-LD still uses full current-output validation and was not optimized or measured by this Quality-disabled scenario.
